w: Raised at the dawn of the 11th century, this basilica is one of three Bordeaux churches -- along with St Andrew's Cathedral and St Michael's Basilica -- written into UNESCO's 1998 listing of the Routes of Santiago de Compostela in France. Pilgrims still pass beneath its stone arches on the road south to Spain.
s: Bordeaux church on UNESCO's Compostela pilgrim road
_facts: Built at the dawn of the 11th century
One of three Bordeaux churches, with St Andrew's Cathedral and St Michael's Basilica, written into UNESCO's 1998 Routes of Santiago de Compostela in France listing

w: Bordeaux's fine-art collection lives in a dependency of the Palais Rohan, five centuries of paintings, sculptures and drawings under one roof. The strongest holdings are French, Flemish and Dutch -- old-master canvases stacked salon-style. Step outside to the Galerie des Beaux-Arts for whatever's showing.
s: Five centuries of French, Flemish and Dutch masters
_facts: Housed in a dependency of the Palais Rohan in central Bordeaux
Collections span the 15th to 20th centuries, strongest in French, Flemish and Dutch painters
The Galerie des Beaux-Arts out front hosts temporary exhibitions

w: One of the largest city squares in Europe, laid out in 1820 on the ruins of the demolished Chateau Trompette -- and built, pointedly, to prevent rebellion, its guns once turned inward toward the city rather than out at it. The trees went in a year earlier, planted in quincunxes, which gave the square its name.
s: A square built, guns inward, to keep Bordeaux in line
_facts: Among the largest city squares in Europe, roughly 63 acres
Laid out in 1820 on the site of the demolished Chateau Trompette, intended to prevent rebellion with its guns turned toward the city
Trees planted in quincunxes in 1818 gave the square its name

w: Completed in 1967, this suspension bridge over the Garonne carries the A630 ring road on a 394-metre main span -- and wears two completely different faces. From the east a ridge lets the roadway glide on almost level; from the flat Medoc side to the west, it has to climb steeply just to reach the same height.
s: One bridge, two totally different approaches
_facts: Large suspension bridge over the Garonne, part of the Bordeaux ring road carrying the A630
Completed in 1967 with a main span of 394 metres
The eastern approach enters nearly level thanks to a ridge; the western approach climbs dramatically across flat Medoc land

w: Once the church of a Benedictine abbey founded in the 7th century, this Romanesque nave went up in the late 11th and early 12th centuries -- four aisles, a polygonal apse, an 18th-century organ. Paul Abadie restored the facade in the 19th century; the old monastery next door now trains Bordeaux's art students.
s: A 7th-century abbey church, now next to an art school
_facts: Formerly the church of a Benedictine abbey founded in the 7th century, built late 11th-early 12th centuries in Romanesque style
Has a nave and four aisles, a transept with apses, a polygonal apse, and an 18th-century organ
Renovated in the 19th century by Paul Abadie; the former abbey now houses the Ecole des beaux-arts de Bordeaux

w: Built in Floirac in 1893, this observatory trained its lenses on a narrow band of sky, between 11 and 17 degrees declination, filling its archives with over 4,000 photographic plates by 1970. It stayed in active use right up to 2016, when the university finally moved its astronomers elsewhere.
s: A century of star-charting from a Floirac hilltop
_facts: Built in Floirac in 1893, affiliated with the University of Bordeaux
Lenses focused between +11 and +17 degrees declination; over 4,000 photographic plates taken by 1970
Actively used until 2016, when the institution moved to a new university location

w: Bordeaux's city hall was built in the 18th century for a rather higher calling -- the Archbishop's Palace, before the Republic requisitioned it for municipal business. It's been running the city ever since, elegant proof that Bordeaux's town clerks work out of an actual palace. Listed as a monument historique in 1997.
s: Bordeaux's city hall used to be the archbishop's palace
_facts: The Hotel de Ville, or City Hall, of Bordeaux, built in the 18th century
Originally served as the Archbishop's Palace of Bordeaux
Designated a monument historique by the French government in 1997

w: Bordeaux's answer to a wine museum, opened in June 2017 with exhibitions, tastings, film screenings and seminars all circling the same subject. It hit a million visitors within eighteen months and passed two million by 2022 -- proof that even a city this soaked in wine still wants to explain itself.
s: Bordeaux explains its own wine obsession, museum-style
_facts: Museum in Bordeaux hosting exhibitions, shows, film screenings and academic seminars centred on wine
Opened in June 2017
Reached one million visitors by autumn 2018 and two million by May 2022

w: The oldest wine estate in Bordeaux, its 700th vintage poured in 2006. Ranked among the Crus Classes for red wine in the 1959 Graves classification -- after being controversially left off the original 1953 list. Seven centuries of harvests in the Pessac-Leognan appellation, and counting.
s: Bordeaux's oldest wine estate, 700 vintages deep
_facts: The oldest wine estate in Bordeaux, harvesting its 700th vintage in 2006
Ranked among the Crus Classes for red wine in the 1959 Graves classification
Omitted from the initial 1953 Graves classification, which caused controversy

w: Henri Fruges hired Le Corbusier in 1924 to build cheap worker housing testing his 1922 manifesto Vers une Architecture -- flat roofs, mass-produced concrete. Costs ballooned three or four times over budget and the workers refused to move in. Fruges sold the houses off; tenants added pitched roofs of their own.
s: Le Corbusier's worker housing that the workers refused
_facts: Commissioned by industrialist Henri Fruges in 1924 as worker housing, designed by Le Corbusier and Pierre Jeanneret
A testing ground for ideas from Le Corbusier's 1922 manifesto Vers une Architecture
Costs ran three to four times over budget; workers refused to move in, forcing Fruges to sell the houses individually
Houses were later heavily modified by owners with pitched roofs and resized windows

w: Charles VII ordered this castle raised at the tail end of the Hundred Years War, to nail down his claim on Bordeaux and the Gascon region -- a fortress built less for show than to make a point stick, and to remind the city exactly who had won.
s: A castle Charles VII built to make his claim on Bordeaux stick
_facts: A castle in Bordeaux built on the orders of Charles VII
Built to secure his claim over Bordeaux and the Gascon region at the end of the Hundred Years War

w: The sister estate to First Growth Chateau Haut-Brion, classed among the Crus Classes in the 1953 Graves ranking. Straddling Talence and Pessac in the Pessac-Leognan appellation, it has poured a second wine, La Chapelle de la Mission, since 1991, plus a dry white absorbed from Chateau Laville Haut-Brion in 2010.
s: First Growth Haut-Brion's lesser-known sister estate
_facts: Sister property of the First Growth Chateau Haut-Brion, classed among the Crus Classes in the 1953 Graves classification
Located in the commune of Talence with additional property in Pessac
Produces a second wine, La Chapelle de la Mission, since 1991, and a dry white since the 2010 merger with Chateau Laville Haut-Brion

w: Bordeaux's Protestant dead have rested here since the cemetery opened in 1826, with the first burial recorded the following March. It grew with the congregation, enlarged in 1867, and picked up a small funerary chapel in 1910 -- a quiet corner of Caudéran still run by the church that founded it two centuries ago.
_facts: Historic church-owned Protestant cemetery inaugurated in 1826 in the district of Caudéran
First burial recorded in March 1827
Enlarged in 1867; a small funerary chapel was added in 1910

w: Landscape architect Le Breton laid out this park in Merignac in 1870, grounds built to flatter the chateau at its centre. Both park and chateau were registered as French national heritage sites on the same day in January 1992 -- a Second Empire garden still doing exactly the job it was designed for.
s: An 1870 landscape garden built around a Mérignac château
_facts: Urban park in the commune of Mérignac, designed by landscape architect Le Breton in 1870
The park and its château were registered as French national heritage sites on 9 January 1992
